acme-sso-admin: Hey team — after rotating our IdP certs yesterday some users can't log in to Redwood. We get 'Recipient check failed' in the SAML response. This started right after the cert rotation. Can someone help?

Sara: Sorry you're hit, thanks for the report. Can you paste the raw SAMLResponse (base64) or a screenshot of the error from the SP logs? Also which ACS URL is configured on the IdP?

acme-sso-admin: I attached the saml response to the ticket (base64). ACS in our metadata is listed as a relative path: `<AssertionConsumerService Location="/sso/acs" Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-POST"/>` — we used that pattern historically. On Redwood side the SP ACS is `https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs`.

Leon: Relative ACS entries can be interpreted differently by IdP/SP implementations. Some libraries resolve them against the entityID while others expect absolute URLs. Recipient check fails when the Recipient in the assertion doesn't exactly match the SP's ACS full URL.

Natalie: Also double-check the certificate in the IdP metadata: after rotation the IdP uploaded a chain and the metadata now contains the intermediate cert instead of the leaf. SP libs will compare the X509Certificate in the metadata to the signature cert thumbprint. If those don't match, signature validation can fail or the SP may reject assertion recipients.

acme-sso-admin: Ugh — that explains why some users hit it and others don't. A few IdPs in our cluster proxy metadata and re-emit the intermediate. How can we confirm?

Sara: Can you run these quick checks and paste outputs?

```
# fetch metadata
curl -sS https://idp.acme/cf-metadata | xmllint --format - | sed -n '1,120p'

# decode SAMLResponse (on a safe machine)
echo "<BASE64>" | base64 --decode | xmllint --format -
```

Leon: In the decoded assertion look for `Recipient`/`Destination` and the `SubjectConfirmationData` attributes. They must exactly match the SP ACS `https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs` (including trailing slash if present). Also confirm `<X509Certificate>` under `KeyDescriptor use=\"signing\"` is the leaf cert (not intermediate).

acme-sso-admin: I ran the metadata fetch and the IdP is indeed publishing the intermediate cert block in `KeyDescriptor use=\"signing\"`. The assertion `Destination` is `https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs` but `SubjectConfirmationData Recipient` is `https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs/` (extra trailing slash).

Natalie: Two separate issues then: cert mismatch and a recipient trailing-slash mismatch. For the cert: either update the IdP metadata to include the correct leaf X509Certificate in the signing KeyDescriptor, or add the intermediate+leaf as separate KeyDescriptor entries in the IdP metadata (best to include the signing cert itself). For the trailing slash: you can either update your IdP to emit the exact Recipient (preferred), or we can temporarily add a tolerant recipient normalization on our side while you fix it — but that requires an enterprise change and audit.

acme-sso-admin: Is there a recommended repro flow so we can test a fix without affecting prod users?

Sara: Yes — create a test SP metadata file pointing to a test ACS endpoint and ask the IdP admin to run a metadata refresh against that test service first. Steps:

1) Generate test SP metadata with exact ACS URL you expect: `https://test-acme.redwood.ai/saml/acs`
2) Upload to IdP staging tenant and rotate their metadata there
3) Attempt login, capture SAMLResponse and verify Recipient + cert via `xmllint`

We also recommend using SAML tracer (browser extension) for quick capture.

devops-bot: Ticket RD-5372 escalated to identity team. Assigned to leon. ETA: initial response 2h.

Leon: I'll take a look. Quick debugging tips I used:

- Check metadata cert with `openssl x509 -in cert.pem -noout -text` and confirm Subject/CN and fingerprint.
- Use `xmlsec1 --verify --pubkey-cert-pem cert.pem <(echo \"$SAML_XML\")` to validate signature if you have the leaf cert.

If the IdP only publishes intermediate in metadata you can still verify signature by fetching the entity's published signing cert from their cert store (if they provide it) or ask them to publish the leaf.

acme-sso-admin: We can push a metadata update with the leaf cert and fix the Recipient trailing slash in staging first. If that works we'll roll to prod. Any logs from Redwood side we should watch?

Sara: If it fails after your change, paste the SP logs for the auth request/response — we look for these errors: `SAMLRecipientMismatch`, `SignatureValidationError`, `InvalidAudience`. Also include the `RequestID` and `InResponseTo` values.

Leon: One more gotcha — some IdPs will canonicalize the ACS during metadata resolution and send `/` appended; others won't. If you have many IdP proxies, normalize by publishing absolute ACS in your metadata. Avoid relative paths.

acme-sso-admin: Great—thanks. We'll try the staging change now and update once done.

(devops-bot): RD-5372 status update: staging metadata update rolled out at 2024-10-02T16:30:00Z to staging idp tenant.

acme-sso-admin: Staging test passed. We pushed the leaf cert and changed ACS to full absolute URL. Prod rollout scheduled in 30m. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:

Sara: Awesome, keep us posted — if you want us to watch the prod rollout we can monitor for `SAMLRecipientMismatch` spikes and rollback guidance.

Leon: After prod rollout, please verify the cert thumbprint in the live metadata matches what you expect: `openssl x509 -in live_cert.pem -fingerprint -sha256 -noout`. We'll close the ticket once we see no failures for 1 hour.

acme-sso-admin: Will do. Thanks!
